source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting company losses in a financial disclosure

1. Start with the accounting records.
2.
completion:
Access the general ledger.
3. Review profit and loss statements.
4. Identify extraordinary items and non-recurring losses.
5. Categorize losses under appropriate headings (e.g., operating losses, asset write-downs, inventory obsolescence, etc.).
6. Verify the accuracy of the figures by cross-referencing with invoices, receipts, and other supporting documents.
7. Make sure to account for tax implications of losses.
8. Document the losses' impact on the financial ratios (e.g., debt-to-equity, liquidity ratios, etc.).
9. Disclose any material losses in the note sections or footnotes to the financial statements.
10. Prepare a detailed narrative that explains the causes of the losses and any related risk factors.
11. Review the disclosures for compliance with applicable financial reporting standards (e.g., IFRS, US GAAP).
12. If necessary, obtain an independent audit or review of the loss disclosure.
